PATHWAY MODULATION: CA-125 reduction (-16.67% vs 0% placebo) suggests biological activity consistent with anti-tumor effect, though this is an indirect measure of DNA repair pathway disruption. 3. CLINICAL TRANSLATION: Strong clinical efficacy with HR 0.35 (95% CI 0.25-0.49, p<0.00001) for progression-free survival demonstrates clear clinical benefit. The large effect size and highly significant p-value indicate robust clinical translation. 4. POPULATION EFFECTS: Trial enrolled platinum-sensitive relapsed serous ovarian cancer patients, a population enriched for homologous recombination deficiency where PARP inhibition mechanism should be most active. No subgroup analysis reported but population selection appears appropriate. 5. CONFOUNDERS: Well-designed placebo-controlled trial with adequate sample size (n=265) and duration, no obvious confounders identified.

failure_modes.evidence: While successful overall, the mechanism of PARP inhibition works best in BRCA-mutated or HRD tumors, suggesting efficacy may be concentrated in a mechanistic subgroup even within this selected population
